text: Motaz Hilal Azaiza, born on 30 January 1999, is a Palestinian photojournalist from Gaza. He was raised in the Deir al-Balah Camp in the then-Israeli-occupied Gaza Strip and attended Al-Azhar University in Gaza, graduating in 2021 with a degree in English studies. As of 2023, he was employed by UNRWA. Prior to the Gaza war, his social media posts focused on daily life in Gaza, and he expressed a desire to be known for his artistic work, aiming to capture the beauty of his people, with a dream of becoming a travel photographer that he could not afford to pursue due to visa costs. Although he covered the 2014 Gaza War and the 2021 Israel–Palestine crisis, his accounts did not gain significant attention at the time, partly due to the lack of foreign journalists in Gaza, as Israel and Egypt denied them access. Before the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, Azaiza had approximately 25,000 followers on Instagram; on 13 October, his account was restricted but access was restored the next day. His follower count grew to one million by 17 October, nine million by October 30, 12.5 million by November 3, and 13 million by November 7, reaching 17.5 million by 27 December and over 18 million by January 2024. On 11 October 2023, at least 15 of his relatives were killed in an Israeli airstrike on the Deir al-Balah Camp. In January 2024, he appeared on Mehdi Hasan's final MSNBC show to discuss the dangers of reporting from Gaza under Israeli bombardment. After 108 days of reporting, he and some family members evacuated to Egypt and then to Doha, Qatar via Al-Arish Airport, marking their first time on a plane. In February 2024, he flew to Istanbul, beginning a series of international travels to "show, tell and speak more," including attending the FIFDH in Geneva, Switzerland, on 8 March, where he participated in a panel with Farah Nabulsi and Mohamed Jabaly at the premiere of Jabaly's film Life is Beautiful. He visited American universities in April, including a Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) panel, and went to London in May to join protests and deliver a speech on Nakba Day. In August, he was invited by English band Massive Attack to speak at their Bristol concert, which drew over 30,000 attendees, and visited Derry, where he was welcomed by mayor Lilian Seenoi-Barr and interviewed by actress Jamie-Lee O'Donnell. In September, he appeared on the BBC News HARDTalk programme. In February 2024, he accepted the 2023 TRT World Citizen Award after arriving in Istanbul. He was featured on Time's list of the 100 most influential people of 2024 in April and awarded the Freedom Prize in Normandy, France in June. He was also one of four Palestinian journalists nominated for the 2024 Nobel Peace Prize. His photograph, "Seeing Her Through My Camera," taken during the Gaza war using a low shutter speed to capture a young girl trapped under rubble at the Al Nusairat refugee camp after an Israeli airstrike, was named one of Time's top 10 photos of 2023 and was featured on Time's list of the 100 most influential people of 2024. In November 2023, GQ Middle East named Azaiza Man of the Year, with editor Ahmad Ali Swaid stating that he reminds people that ordinary individuals have the power to enact change. In a February 2024 interview with The Guardian, Azaiza described experiencing traumatic flashbacks, guilt, and hopelessness after leaving Gaza.
